newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia warned of electronic money fraud crisis.
newsitem.headline: Australia warned of electronic money fraud crisis.

text.p: Australia could be "dangerously exposed" to illegal transactions by organised criminals using local electronic money systems to transfer billions of dollars, a leading criminal lawyer said on Thursday.

"The ability to hide one's financial tracks under cover of electronic anonymity has been, and will be, very greatly enhanced by technology," Frank Costigan QC told a crime and corruption conference in Brisbane.
"Failure to allow the National Crime Authority (the nation's top crime investigator) to continue its work in this area would leave this country dangerously exposed," he said.

Costigan, the former head of a Royal Commission into police corruption and an architect of the National Crime Authority's formation, said sophisticated techniques in electronic money transfer "rendered even more difficult" the checks on money laundering in Australia.
"A weakening of its (NCA) capacity to monitor money laundering would act as a global invitation to come to Australia for this purpose," he said.
The single most effective tool in the NCA's armoury was its ability to follow money trails, he said.
"The attack on organised crime will come to nought unless an effective mechanism for following the money trail is maintained and provided to a body such as the NCA," Costigan said.
